title: Compactly supported direct image of towers is computed levelwise
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Write $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$, so $R_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n=A_{E,en}$. Use the varying-coefficient tower category and its derived evaluations of [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Let $c=(j,p)$ be a compactification $f=pj:X\to Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and define $F_f=Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$ on $D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(X,\mathcal O_E))$. Then:

1. There is a natural comparison $(F_fC)_n\simeq Rp_{*,R_n}j_{!,R_n}C_n=Rf_{!,R_n}^{c}C_n$ for every bounded-below tower complex $C$.
2. The following specified operations and maps exist in the ordinary derived categories of varying-coefficient towers and evaluate to the finite operations and maps. Tensor means derived tensor over the ring system $(R_{n,T})_n$; no completed tensor or condensed coefficient identification is meant.
   (a) In the global field setting $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p_0}$, $\ell\ne p_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], let $f$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes. For bounded-below towers $K$ on $X$ and $L$ on $Y$ whose levels are pro-etale realizations of bounded constructible finite-Tor complexes, with specified etale-origin witnesses at each level [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], the compactification projection map
   $F_fK\otimes^L_{R_{\bullet,Y}}L\longrightarrow F_f(K\otimes^L_{R_{\bullet,X}}f^{-1}L)$
   is an isomorphism. Both $K_n$ and $L_n$ are required to satisfy the finite-Tor hypothesis. The formula is formed in the ambient unbounded tower derived category using the total derived operations; on the bounded-below domain $F_f$ is the functor above.
   (b) For a cartesian compact-support square [def-cbc-compact-support-square], with separated finite-type $f$, arbitrary $g:Y'\to Y$, and compactification $c'=(j',p')$ obtained by base change from $c$, the specified exchange
   $g^{-1}F_fC\longrightarrow F_{f'}g'^{-1}C$
   is an isomorphism for $C\in D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(X,\mathcal O_E))$ whose every level has an etale-origin witness. There is no requirement that the chosen witnesses themselves be a compatible tower.
   (c) For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $a:U\hookrightarrow T$, and every $C\in D^+(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$, the open counit and closed unit fit into a distinguished triangle
   $a_{!,\bullet}a^{-1}C\to C\to i_{*,\bullet}i^{-1}C\to a_{!,\bullet}a^{-1}C[1]$.
   This evaluates to the finite open–closed triangle. The exact immersion operations in this formula are applied termwise. On schemes where $\ell$ is invertible, the same evaluation assertions include tensoring with specified coefficient-twist towers, that is, towers whose levels are the finite Tate twists with their quotient transitions [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].
3. A morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E))$ is an isomorphism if and only if all its derived evaluations are isomorphisms. This assertion is for the unbounded ordinary derived category and asserts conservativity, not faithfulness or existence of lifts of arbitrary families of derived maps.

proof.text: For clause 1, [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] gives exact degreewise pro-etale $j_!$ and its compatibility with restriction of finite coefficients. Thus it acts on strict towers and complexes with $(j_{!,\bullet}C)_n=j_!C_n$. Its exactness follows componentwise from [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian], so it preserves the lower bound. Apply [det-sp-tower-injective-components] to the bounded-below complex $j_{!,\bullet}C$: its derived direct-image comparison gives $(Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}C)_n\simeq Rp_*j_!C_n$. This is exactly clause 1, naturally in $C$.

source.place: (1): exact extension by zero followed by the injective-components comparison

proof.text: Prove clause 3 before using it. Exact derived evaluation is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. For an actual derived tower morphism $v$, let $D$ be a cone. If every $v_n$ is invertible, its evaluated distinguished triangle has zero third term by [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero], so $\mathcal H^r(D)_n=0$ for every $r,n$. Evaluation commutes with cohomology because kernels and cokernels are levelwise and evaluation is exact [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Therefore every cohomology tower of $D$ is zero, hence $D$ is the zero object of the derived category and the same cone criterion makes $v$ invertible. Conversely, a functor sends a morphism and its inverse to mutually inverse maps. This detects isomorphisms of already constructed morphisms; it is not an assertion that evaluation is faithful.

source.place: (3): cone argument for arbitrary derived morphisms

proof.text: Use the fixed small pro-etale sites underlying [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] and the strict ring systems $B_n=(R_n)_T$, with the actual quotient homomorphisms. Its tower category is exactly $\mathscr S(B)$ of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]: both have $B_n$-modules and semilinear transitions, not modules over a fixed ring. That node identifies its enhanced localization with coherent semilinear sections, over all evaluations, and gives simultaneous derived tensor, inverse image, right derived direct image, open extension, units and counits on these section models. In particular its scope is all unbounded complexes, without flat quotient maps and without normalized inputs. For $m\geq n$, write $T_{mn}=-\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n$ and $t^C_{mn}:T_{mn}C_m\to C_n$ for the transition adjunct. The tensor transition is $T_{mn}(K_m\otimes^L L_m)\simeq T_{mn}K_m\otimes^LT_{mn}L_m\xrightarrow{t^K_{mn}\otimes t^L_{mn}}K_n\otimes^LL_n$. The associator is the derived tensor/pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the identity underlying topos and the ring quotient. The coherent models in the section lemma supply the composition homotopies for all $m\geq n\geq r$. Thus evaluation of the actual derived tower tensor is $K_n\otimes^L_{R_n}L_n$, including its transition data, rather than merely evaluation of the underived tensor. This also applies when one input is a specified twist tower.

source.place: (2): levelwise flatness/tensor assertion replaced by the coherent varying-ring derived calculus

proof.text: Construct the specified maps using [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], not by lifting a family of finite derived maps. For a geometric inverse image $V=u^{-1}$ with right derived adjoint $G=Ru_*$, its coefficient comparison $b_{mn}:T_{mn}G_m\to G_nT_{mn}$ is the counit transpose of $V_nT_{mn}G_m\simeq T_{mn}V_mG_m\xrightarrow{T_{mn}\varepsilon_m}T_{mn}$; hence the transition of $G(C)$ is $G_n(t^C_{mn})b_{mn}$. The section lemma gives this specified counit transpose, the coherent section adjunction, and evaluation of its units and counits. Form the projection transformation by the compactification formula of [def-exchange-projection]: the proper counit-tensor transpose $\pi_p$ followed by $Rp_*$ of the canonical open tensor comparison. Only that definition's projection clause is used (take its auxiliary $g=\operatorname{id}_Y$); its extra finite-type assumption on that auxiliary map imposes no restriction on the arbitrary base map in part (b). Form the compact-support exchange by the formula in [def-cbc-exchange-map]: $\eta_{p'}$, then $Rp'_*$ of the pullback square identification, then $Rp'_*\bar g'^{-1}\varepsilon_p$, followed by $Rp'_*$ of the open base-change comparison. The section lemma explicitly supplies coherent models for these mates, open-adjunction comparisons and composites. Its preservation of evaluation, composition and transposes says that evaluating these exact formulas yields the finite specified $\operatorname{PF}^c$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c$, including their adjunction normalization. Coefficient-transition compatibility thus comes from the coherent geometric constructions just cited, rather than from naturality at one fixed coefficient ring. The derived tower direct image here restricts to $Rp_{*,\bullet}$ on $D^+$: it is the right adjoint of the same exact termwise inverse image, with the canonical derived adjunction, and clause 1 identifies its finite evaluations.

source.place: (2): construction and evaluation of the projection and base-change mates

proof.text: At each level of part (a), the ring is the finite ring $R_n=A_{E,en}$, and BOTH inputs are bounded constructible finite-Tor etale realizations with witnesses. Thus [sk-thm-sf-pf-proetale] makes the evaluated projection transformation invertible. At each level of part (b), exact evaluation preserves bounded-below inputs; the ring is finite commutative, $f$ is separated finite type, the square is cartesian with arbitrary $g$, and the input has its specified etale-origin witness. Therefore [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] makes the evaluated exchange invertible. These theorems are applied only after step 4 constructs the actual tower maps and identifies their evaluations. Clause 3 (step 2) now makes each tower map invertible. No compatibility of the witnesses is used to build the maps, since those were constructed from geometric tower adjunctions before witnesses were used to test invertibility.

For part (c), choose ONE bounded-below representative complex $C^\cdot$ in the abelian category of towers. For every degree $q$ and level $n$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with ring sheaf $(R_n)_T$ to $C_n^q$, using the assumed quasi-compactness of $a$. It gives $0\to a_!a^{-1}C_n^q\to C_n^q\to i_*i^{-1}C_n^q\to0$, whose maps are the open counit and closed unit. They commute with the differentials by naturality. They also commute with the semilinear transitions: restriction of the scalar action does not change the underlying inverse/direct image maps or these topoi units and counits; open extension commutes with finite-ring restriction of scalars by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Applying naturality to $C_m^q\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}C_n^q$ therefore gives the transition squares. By [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian] these are a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes of towers. [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] produces its distinguished triangle. The immersion functors here are exact (open extension and closed direct image by the ringed open–closed lemma, inverse images by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]); [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identifies their derived operations with these termwise ones. Finally, exact evaluation is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], so it carries this triangle, with its counit and unit, to the same finite open–closed triangle. No short exact sequence of abstract derived objects, or gluing of unrelated distinguished triangles, is asserted.
